data.name: Julaybib
data.gender_notes: Julaybib is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'l-b-b' meaning 'lion'. Julaybib is a name given to a young and courageous man. In Islamic history, Julaybib ibn Al-Harith was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and participated in several battles. He is known for his bravery and loyalty. The name Julaybib carries the meaning “Young lion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Julaybib usually hope their child will grow to embody young lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, courage, and loyalty in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Julaybib belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Young lion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Julaybib total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: جليبب

historical_references.reference: Al-Tabari, Ibn Abd al-Hakam and Ibn Kathir all reported that Julaybib ibn Al-Harith al-Kindi was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad and a member of the Muhajirun (emigrants) who fled Mecca for Medina. He was one of the ten Muhajirun who were martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 625 AD.

Al-Tabari also reported that Julaybib was one of the commanders of the Prophet's army in the Battle of Hunayn in 630 AD. During the battle, the Prophet Muhammad asked Julaybib to lead the right flank of the army, and Julaybib's bravery and leadership were instrumental in the Muslim victory.
